title: Research: a built-in browser per project that agents can drive
notes:
Research only, no code. Design a browser inside Dashboard that Claude sessions and workers can control, and split it into buildable cards.
Goals, in order: (1) a preview per card worktree (the worker's dev server shown on the project's page), (2) the PR and CI pages beside the review loop, (3) before/after screenshots attached to a UI PR. General browsing behind per-project logins comes after.
Questions to answer with evidence (file:line, Electron docs URLs):
- View: WebContentsView per project/pane; how it fits the page and modes (PROJECT_MODES, ACTIONS, page.ts, focusMode, modeLabel, help.ts; keys-rule-1/2, conventions-rule-1 keyboard first); how window-navigation.ts keeps the main window locked while the view browses; per-project session partitions.
- Control: an MCP server in main driving only that view through webContents.debugger (CDP), reached through the dashboard command socket; never --remote-debugging-port (it would expose the app window and terminals). Tool set and token cost: navigate, snapshot (accessibility tree or trimmed text), click, type, screenshot, console, network. How screens/workers get it (as chat-chrome.ts adds --chrome).
- Overlap: what Claude in Chrome and the Playwright MCP plugin already cover; what only the built-in browser can do.
- Demand: count browser tool use (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*, mcp__plugin_playwright*, WebFetch) in the session logs under ~/.claude/projects/*dashboard* and other projects' dirs over the last 30 days.
- Risks: a page reaching the app window, sites blocking embedded browsers (Google sign-in), Electron upgrade churn, no DOM test environment.
Deliver: a comment on this card with the design, the cards to build (each S/M/L, in order, with what each one makes testable), the demand count, and a recommendation (build, build only goal 1, or don't).

comments.body:
RESULT — built-in browser research (read-only, 2026-11-20)

RECOMMENDATION: build only goal 1, and only its human half first (cards 1-3). Hold the agent-control MCP (card 4) until a worker actually asks for it; drop goals 2 and 3 as built-in-browser work.
Why: the demand that exists is for real logged-in sites in Chrome (job boards, a staging site), which Claude in Chrome already serves and an embedded browser does worse; localhost previews are 33 navigations in 30 days across six projects, and Playwright MCP already drives those headless. What only Dashboard can add is a person seeing the worker's dev server on the project's page.

DEMAND (tool_use blocks deduped by id, *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects modified in the last 30 days, 7,553 files)
- Claude in Chrome 2,144 · Playwright MCP 425 · WebFetch 1,053
- by project: insta-experiences 1,283 (chrome 1,093) · job-search 1,001 (chrome 794) · raxel-lead-machine 798 (WebFetch 766) · new-crm 172 · dahua 141 · kamandsystem 65 · dotfiles 56 · dashboard itself 25 (playwright 10, WebFetch 15)
- browser navigations: 351, of which 33 to localhost (kamandsystem 14, new-crm 10, raxel-studio 4, lead-machine 2, dashboard 2, habit-tracker 1). The rest are signed-in sites: test8.exp.instacoins.travel 26, jobs.ashbyhq.com 17, linkedin, greenhouse...
- github.com: 56 WebFetch calls; PR/CI is already read through gh by the review loop.

DESIGN
View
- One WebContentsView per project (Electron 45.2.1, package.json:42; WebContentsView replaced the deprecated BrowserView in Electron 30: https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents-view, https://www.electronjs.org/blog/electron-30-0). Added to window.contentView, bounds set from a placeholder element in a new 'browser' view of page.ts through a ResizeObserver + IPC.
- A new mode, per keys-rule-1: 'browser' in PROJECT_MODES (src/shared/keys/modes.ts:7), a row in ACTIONS (src/shared/keys/actions.ts), a view in page.ts (makeView, page.ts:296; showMode toggles hidden, page.ts:230-233), a branch in focusMode (renderer.ts:378) and modeLabel (src/renderer/app/status.ts), name + blurb in src/renderer/keys/help.ts. showMode's `hidden` does nothing to a native view: main must also setVisible(false) it, so "is the view on screen" is a decision module with a test (mode is browser AND no HTML overlay — help, picker, which-key, PDF viewer — is up, because a native view draws over all HTML).
- Keyboard first: once the view has focus the renderer hears no keys. The existing before-input-event hook on every contents (app-window.ts:36-39) is where mode keys and the leader get forwarded to the window; which keys leave the view is a decision module + test. Mode keys pass through: the browser mode key pressed in browser mode goes to the page. Links/rows on the page are the site's own; Dashboard keys are address bar (a row the arrows walk: back, forward, reload, url), not buttons.
- Navigation lock: today the view could not load anything. app.on('web-contents-created') applies frameNavigation to every contents (app-window.ts:32-55), and a main frame that is not the window's goes to the system browser or is refused (window-navigation.ts:16-18); setWindowOpenHandler denies every popup. frameNavigation needs a third frame kind, isBrowserView, allowed http(s) in its main frame; popups open in the same view. The window's own will-navigate lock (app-window.ts:134-136, windowMayNavigate window-navigation.ts:26) is untouched, so the app page still can't be replaced.
- Isolation: the view gets no preload, sandbox: true, contextIsolation, and session.fromPartition('persist:browser-<project name>') (https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/session#sessionfrompartitionpartition-options), so cookies are per project and never in the app's default session. With no preload there is no bridge for a page to call; ipcMain handlers still should check event.sender is the window's contents (https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security#17-validate-the-sender-of-all-ipc-messages).

Control (card 4, deferred)
- Main drives only that view with webContents.debugger.attach('1.3') + sendCommand (https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/debugger): Page.navigate, Accessibility.getFullAXTree, Input.dispatchMouseEvent/insertText, Page.captureScreenshot, Runtime.consoleAPICalled / Network.* events. Never --remote-debugging-port: it serves every target, the app window and its terminals included.
- Reach: worker screens run their query() in the screen-host process (chat-sessions.ts:340, src/main/workers/screen-host-*.ts), not main, so an in-process SDK MCP server would live in the wrong process. Instead a stdio server, `dashboard browser-mcp`, passed as options.mcpServers beside the existing extraArgs chrome flag (chat-sessions.ts:303-304, chat-chrome.ts), forwarding each call over DASHBOARD_SOCKET like the other app commands (src/main/command/reach-app.ts). Plain data, so it crosses to the screen host.
- Tools: navigate, snapshot, click(ref), type(ref,text), screenshot, console(last N), network(last N). Cost: a screenshot is about width*height/750 tokens (https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/vision), ~1,400 at 1280x800. A full AX tree of a big page is unmeasured here but large; snapshot must be a trimmed tree (roles+names+refs, capped). Seven small schemas sit in every turn's context of every session that gets the server, so only workers that ask get it.
- Overlap: Claude in Chrome (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome; already wired, chat-chrome.ts) drives the user's real Chrome with their logins. Playwright MCP (https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp) launches its own Chromium, headless or not, with --isolated per session, and has every tool above plus screenshots. Only the built-in one shows the page on the project's page, beside the panes, in the same window the person is looking at.

RISKS (each with what happens)
- Page reaching the app: without the frameNavigation change the view's first load is sent to the system browser; with a too-wide change (allowing any main frame) a PDF viewer contents could load remote sites in the overlay. Keep the rule keyed on the view's contents identity, tested in window-navigation.test.ts.
- Native view over HTML: press the help key while browsing and the dialog opens under the page, invisible, while keys go to it. The visibility module above is the fix and the thing to hand-check.
- Embedded sign-in: Google refuses OAuth in embedded user agents ("disallowed_useragent"; https://developers.googleblog.com/2016/08/modernizing-oauth-interactions-in-native-apps.html), so any Google-login site never signs in. That is most of the "general browsing" demand above. GitHub sign-in works in embedded Chromium in my experience but I have no source for it.
- Electron churn: WebContentsView is two years old and BrowserView's removal already happened once; debugger protocol '1.3' is stable CDP. Moderate.
- No DOM test environment: bounds, focus and z-order are by-hand checks only; the testable parts are the three decision modules named below.
- File size: renderer.ts is 924 lines and page.ts 704 (total, not code-only; check against max-lines before adding). The browser wiring goes in its own renderer/browser/ module, not into either.
- Preview ports: two card worktrees running `pnpm dev` collide on one port; the preview card needs the worker to say which URL, not Dashboard guessing.
- Goal 3 snag: I found no documented GitHub REST endpoint for attaching an image to a PR comment; screenshots would have to be committed or hosted. That problem is the same with Playwright, so it is not a reason for a built-in browser.

CARDS (in order)
1. S — frameNavigation knows a browser-view contents: http(s) allowed in its main frame, popups into the same view, window lock unchanged. Testable: window-navigation.test.ts cases for each frame kind.
2. M — Browser mode: per-project WebContentsView with its own persist partition, sandboxed, no preload; placeholder bounds; address-bar row; mode wiring (PROJECT_MODES, ACTIONS, page view, focusMode, modeLabel, help.ts blurb, docs). Testable: browser-visibility (mode + overlay -> shown) and browser-keys (which keys leave the view) modules with tests; the rest by hand.
3. S — `dashboard browser open <url> [--project]` through the socket, calling an action in src/main/actions/browser/ (actions-rule-1); worker instructions say to run it after starting a dev server. Makes goal 1 work end to end: the card's dev server shows on the project's page. Testable: CLI argument decision + action test.
4. M (hold) — `dashboard browser-mcp` stdio server + CDP driver in main, seven tools, trimmed snapshot. Testable: AX-tree trimming and ref->node resolution as pure modules. Build when a worker's need for it shows up (e.g. Playwright can't see what the person sees).
5. L (don't, for now) — one view per card worktree instead of per project; PR/CI pages; screenshots attached to PRs. gh and Playwright already cover the agent side.
